Remark #1: The map cluster block begins directly after the FAT table
FAT Table: The FAT table contains items of 8 bytes, being split into:
a 32-bit upper segment and 32-bit lower offset
with them referencing on a per-cluster basis.
The address is meant to reference a cluster in reserved space: the base extension cluster

Base extension cluster.Security Code: A 15 byte code that is used to validate the associated cluster.
Base extension cluster.num_extensions: A byte describing how many additional clusters are used as part of the addressing cluster.
Base extension cluster.FAT: This is the pointer to the FAT entry of the associated file.

Creation Time.Upper 15 bits: Hours: 5 bits, Minutes: 6 bits, Seconds: 5 bits

Modified Time.Upper 15 bits: Hours: 5 bits, Minutes: 6 bits, Seconds: 5 bits

Base extension cluster.name len: The length of the file's name

cluster_entries.Is file: An array of addresses pointing to the clusters that make up the associated file
Is directory: An array of FAT indexes, as in the FAT index.
It makes use of the segment and offset as addresses.

drive.Security Code: A 15 byte code that is used to validate the associated cluster.
drive.prev_header: The address of the previous header, ignorable if this header is the 1st header.
drive.next_header: The address of the next header, ignorable if last header.

MAP cluster.pad: A byte used to round-up to 32 bytes
MAP cluster.data: Array of bytes that make up the rest of the cluster
